ProtT5 Ubiquitination Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: ProtT5_ubiquitination_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Embeddings: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 • 1024-dim  |  Task: binary protein-level ubiquitination classification

1. Dataset

Proteins from UniProt/Swiss-Prot split using the Post-translational modification column:

  • Positive (ubiquitinated): PTM field contains "ubiquitin" (case-insensitive)
  • Negative (not ubiquitinated): PTM field does not mention ubiquitin

2. Methods

2.1 Embeddings

ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 (1024-dim) embeddings, max pooling and attention pooling. All features z-score normalised.

2.2 Classifiers

ModelArchitecture / SettingsImbalance handling
Logistic RegressionL2, max_iter=5000class_weight="balanced"
MLP (PyTorch)Linear(1024→512)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(512→256)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(256→1), Adam lr=1e-3, 30 epochs, batch=64 BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight=neg/pos

80/20 stratified train/test split, seed 42.

5. Interpretation

5.1 MLP vs Logistic Regression

MLP attn PR-AUC: 0.2775  |  MLP max PR-AUC: 0.2687
LR attn PR-AUC: 0.2457  |  LR max PR-AUC: 0.1682

5.2 Cross-Model Context

ProtT5-XL uses 1024-dim embeddings, between Ankh (768-dim) and ESM-2 (1280-dim). Compare results_ubiquitination_ProtT5/, results_ubiquitination_ESM2/, and results_ubiquitination_Ankh/ for a three-way model comparison.

5.3 UMAP vs PCA / t-SNE

UMAP preserves global structure better than t-SNE at scale. Substantial overlap between classes is expected for protein-level pooled representations.

5.4 Recommendations

  1. Residue-level classifier on ProtT5 token embeddings
  2. 5-fold stratified cross-validation instead of single split
  3. Concatenate max + attention pool (2×1024) as joint feature
  4. Ensemble ProtT5, ESM2 and Ankh embeddings
  5. Fine-tune ProtT5 end-to-end on the ubiquitination task
